recommendations.text: Arterial blood gases and chest X-ray should be obtained
For COPD Exacerbation Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - assess vital signs (within 10 minutes) - assess respiratory status - order lab abg - order imaging chest xray
NIV in pneumothorax causes tension pneumothorax. [FORBIDDEN: initiate_niv, initiate_bipap, initiate_cpap] (Severity: CRITICAL)
High FiO2 in CO2 retainers worsens hypercapnia via Haldane effect. [FORBIDDEN: give_high_flow_oxygen_100pct, give_high_fio2] (Severity: HIGH)
Facial trauma prevents mask seal for NIV. [FORBIDDEN: initiate_niv, initiate_bipap] (Severity: HIGH)
Non-selective beta-blockers cause bronchospasm in COPD. [FORBIDDEN: give_nonselective_beta_blocker, give_propranolol] (Severity: HIGH)
Macrolides and ciprofloxacin increase theophylline levels causing toxicity. [FORBIDDEN: add_macrolide_without_theophylline_check, give_ciprofloxacin] (Severity: MODERATE)
Cor pulmonale patients are preload-sensitive; aggressive fluids cause RV failure. [FORBIDDEN: give_aggressive_iv_fluids, give_large_volume_fluid] (Severity: HIGH)
COPD-CHF overlap: do not increase beta-blocker during acute exacerbation. [FORBIDDEN: increase_beta_blocker, give_high_dose_beta_blocker] (Severity: HIGH)
AKI/CKD patients need steroid dose adjustment and NSAID avoidance. [FORBIDDEN: give_high_dose_methylprednisolone, give_nsaid] (Severity: HIGH)
Bronchodilators, systemic corticosteroids, and antibiotics should be initiated promptly
For Severe COPD Exacerbation, the following actions are mandatory: - give bronchodilator (within 30 minutes) - give systemic corticosteroid - give antibiotics - assess niv eligibility - order lab abg
During Severe COPD Exacerbation, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give sedatives, give high flow o2 without monitoring.
